chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, raising it (mursal), from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
Had the people known what is in seeking knowledge, they would seek it even if it were by spilling their lifeblood and diving into the ocean depths.

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to Daniel: The most detestable of My servants to Me is the ignorant one who takes lightly the rights of the people of knowledge, the one who neglects following them; and that the most beloved of My servants to Me is the pious one, the seeker of abundant reward, the one who stays close to scholars, who follows the forbearing ones, and who accepts from the wise.

key_terms.الاقتداء: Following/emulating — religious imitation of scholars as authoritative guides
key_terms.الحكماء: The wise ones — those with deep discernment and understanding
key_terms.الحلماء: The forbearing ones — those who exercise patience and clemency in knowledge transmission
key_terms.اللجج: Ocean depths — plural of لُجَّة (lujja), the deep parts of the sea; metaphor for extreme difficulty
key_terms.المستخف بحق أهل العلم: One who belittles the rights of scholars — a severe description of negligence toward religious knowledge
key_terms.سفك المهج: Spilling lifeblood — extreme hyperbole for the price one should pay for knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the reward of seeking knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-'Abidin (the fourth Imam, grandson of Imam Ali) transmits this teaching emphasizing the supreme importance of seeking religious knowledge, using vivid hyperbole of sacrificing one's blood and diving into seas. The second part cites a divine revelation to the Prophet Daniel, contrasting the most despised servant (the ignorant person who disrespects scholars) with the most beloved (the pious person who diligently follows scholars, the forbearing, and the wise). This hadith was addressed to a community navigating religious life without direct access to the Imams, emphasizing that adherence to qualified scholars was a divine imperative.
word_analysis: the one who adheres/stays close to
